primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 10121, Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010
relevant_provisions: Sections 6 and 9 assign the NDRRMC and Office of Civil Defense (OCD) responsibility for national standards, the DRRM information system, national early warning, information-sharing procedures, inter-council communications, and the 24-hour NDRRM Operations Center.

Sections 11 and 12 assign local councils and LDRRM offices authority within territorial jurisdiction: councils approve, monitor, and evaluate local DRRM plans and recommend forced or pre-emptive evacuation; LDRRM offices consolidate risk information, operate local multi-hazard early warning, monitor disasters, maintain operational databases, implement approved policies, and submit prescribed fund-utilization reports.

The Act permits private-sector participation and partnerships, but does not transfer the statutory decision authority of NDRRMC, OCD, local chief executives, local councils, or LDRRM offices to a vendor.

primary_sources.source: NDRRM Operations Center Standard Operating Procedures and Guidelines, 2024 Edition
relevant_provisions: The SOPG defines NDRRMOC operating, alert, warning, coordination, and reporting workflows rather than a general software specification.

Its warning-dissemination matrix routes advisories received from official warning agencies through prescribed OCD/NDRRMC channels such as the OCD SMS Blast System, NDRRMC Monitoring Dashboard, Emergency Alert and Warning Messages, email, and Viber, with triggers and templates developed with warning agencies.

The workflow supports a system design that preserves source agency, receipt time, dissemination channel, recipients, version, operator, and approval/escalation events; it does not support autonomous generation or alteration of official warnings by a startup product.

primary_sources.source: DILG Operation L!STO Disaster Preparedness Manuals and program materials
relevant_provisions: Operation L!STO translates preparedness duties into minimum actions and checklists for local chief executives and LGUs, including institutional structures, competencies, resource mobilization, and hazard-specific preparedness actions.

For this paper, L!STO is an operational benchmark for checklist coverage and evidence capture; it is not independent legal authority for a private system to issue warnings, order evacuation, certify compliance, or replace the accountable public official.

primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 8792, Electronic Commerce Act of 2000
relevant_provisions: Sections 6 to 13 recognize electronic data messages, documents, and signatures, but evidential weight turns on reliable generation, storage, communication, originator identification, integrity, accessibility, accurate representation, and date/time information.

Sections 18 to 22 address attribution, duplicate messages, errors, acknowledgement, dispatch, and receipt; these support explicit identities, designated inboxes, acknowledgements, duplicate detection, and immutable transmission logs.

Section 27 authorizes government electronic transactions subject to agency-adopted rules specifying format, signatures, control procedures, integrity, security, and confidentiality. Electronic form alone therefore does not make a startup record an approved official filing.

primary_sources.source: Republic Act No. 9470, National Archives of the Philippines Act of 2007
relevant_provisions: Sections 6 and 9 place government-wide public-record creation, protection, use, storage, preservation, access, transfer, and disposition standards under the National Archives of the Philippines (NAP).

Sections 15 to 21 require agency registries and approved disposition schedules; public records cannot be destroyed without prior written authority, and electronic records may remain with the controlling office when the NAP Executive Director so instructs.
Sections 30 to 37 make access classification and restrictions decisions of the controlling government office and NAP, not the software provider.
Sections 3 to 6 promote whole-of-government interoperability and private-sector/startup participation while retaining agency mandates and placing harmonization and standards leadership with DICT.

Section 9 requires an integrated government network, a Philippine Government Interoperability Framework, and records workflows covering creation through disposal, plus secure APIs for common datasets.

Sections 10 to 13 require privacy impact assessment, minimum information-security standards, security testing for critical information infrastructure, incident reporting, and public-service continuity.

Sections 16, 18, 19, and 23 to 24 keep agency heads and CIOs accountable, require nondigital alternatives and inclusive access, restrict government-system access to duly authorized officers and agents, and require risk-proportionate security for systems operated by contractors on an agency's behalf.

evidence_quality_and_caveats.quality: RA 10121, RA 8792, RA 9470, and RA 12254 are primary Philippine statutes. The 2024 SOPG is an official NDRRMC/OCD operational issuance. Operation L!STO material is official DILG program guidance but is not a statute.
evidence_quality_and_caveats.applicability: The statutes establish minimum authority and lifecycle boundaries nationwide. Exact report forms, approval chains, retention periods, access classes, warning triggers, and interfaces remain dependent on current NDRRMC/OCD/DILG/DICT/NAP issuances, the adopting LGU's ordinances and records-disposition schedule, and the executed government contract.
caveats: Legal recognition of an electronic record is not the same as automatic authenticity, admissibility, official acceptance, or evidential weight; those depend on integrity, attribution, procedure, and agency rules.
Interoperability duties do not create unrestricted data-sharing authority and remain subject to privacy, confidentiality, security, records, and agency-mandate limits.
The sources do not establish that automation improves disaster outcomes, reporting accuracy, or response time; those are empirical claims requiring field evaluation.
Operation L!STO manuals vary by hazard and edition, so a requirements baseline must identify the exact customer-adopted manual and revision before compliance testing.

scope_inclusions: A multi-tenant startup service for authorized LGU/LDRRMO personnel to capture, validate, version, route, acknowledge, consolidate, search, export, and audit disaster preparedness and incident records.
Configurable role-based workflows reflecting barangay, municipal/city, provincial, regional, and national reporting paths without changing the legal authority attached to each office.
Source-labelled ingestion of official hazard advisories and warnings, with verbatim preservation, timestamps, delivery status, and links or identifiers back to the issuing warning agency.
Operation L!STO-aligned preparedness checklists and evidence attachments when the customer identifies the applicable manual, hazard, and edition.

Electronic signatures or approvals, audit trails, record version history, acknowledgement, duplicate/error controls, retention labels, legal hold, export, and disposition workflows configured to agency rules.
Standards-based import/export and documented APIs for authorized government interoperability, plus offline or low-connectivity capture and accessible/manual fallback paths.
Service responsibilities for availability monitoring, backups, tested restoration, tenant isolation, access logging, security incident handling, portability, and orderly offboarding.

exclusions: Issuing, rewriting, or certifying official hazard warnings independently of PAGASA, PHIVOLCS, OCD/NDRRMC, or another legally authorized warning agency.

Autonomously ordering evacuation, declaring a state of calamity, approving a DRRM plan, authorizing fund use, certifying regulatory compliance, or making final resource-allocation or incident-command decisions.
Replacing NDRRMC/OCD reporting systems, PhilAWARE, official government repositories, NAP authority, or the agency's records officer unless formally designated and integrated under applicable rules.
Promising that system records are automatically admissible, authentic, public, permanent, or legally sufficient merely because they are electronic.
Destroying, anonymizing, publishing, or transferring public records solely on vendor policy or a user click.
dependencies: A written data-processing/service agreement, agency authorization matrix, designated approvers, approved forms and reporting timelines, records-disposition schedule, access classification, incident-response contacts, and offboarding plan.

DICT interoperability, security, privacy-impact, and accessibility requirements; NAP records-management rules; relevant National Privacy Commission rules; customer ordinances and SOPs; and current NDRRMC/OCD/DILG issuances.
Reliable official source feeds or designated human entry, connectivity or store-and-forward capability, trained staff, and government validation of imported and consolidated information.
scope_exclusions_and_dependencies.non_claims: The startup is a workflow and recordkeeping processor/support provider, not the disaster authority, warning originator, records custodian by default, or substitute for professional and accountable human judgment.

objective_requirements_and_metrics.objective: Preserve provenance and human accountability across the report lifecycle.
measures: Percentage of test records retaining source office, named originator, role, creation/receipt time, verification state, approver, version, and every status transition
Target: 100% in scripted lifecycle tests; no record can enter an approved/final state without an authorized human approval event

objective_requirements_and_metrics.objective: Demonstrate electronic-record integrity and reproducible export.
measures: Tamper-evidence tests detect modification of finalized content or audit events
Export/re-import comparison preserves content, identifiers, timestamps, attachments, signatures/approval evidence, and checksums
Target: 100% detection of the defined tamper cases and 100% field/attachment reconciliation in the test corpus

objective_requirements_and_metrics.objective: Support prescribed reporting without claiming authority over it.
measures: Map each customer-approved NDRRMC/OCD/LGU field and routing step to the system schema
Target: 100% coverage of the agreed sample forms and zero unauthorized-role submissions in permission tests
Compare median completion time and correction rate against the customer's existing process using the same scenarios; report effect size and confidence intervals rather than presuming improvement
Publish versioned schema/API documentation and export a non-proprietary machine-readable package plus human-readable rendition
Target: 100% successful validation against the agreed schema and complete tenant export within the contractual recovery-time objective
Test idempotency and duplicate detection using repeated submissions and delayed acknowledgements

objective_requirements_and_metrics.objective: Maintain service continuity and inclusion during disruptions.
measures: Measure recovery time, recovery point, backup restoration success, offline queue reconciliation, and accessibility against contractually approved thresholds
Target: zero silent data loss in interruption tests, 100% successful restoration in scheduled drills, and no critical WCAG/Philippine Web Accessibility defects in the tested workflows
Retain a documented manual fallback and verify it in an operational exercise

objective_requirements_and_metrics.objective: Enforce retention, access, and disposition authority.
measures: Target: 100% denial of cross-tenant and unauthorized-role access in the defined test matrix
No final disposal without the configured records-officer approval and required NAP/agency authority
Every view, export, classification change, legal hold, retention change, and disposition is logged and reviewable

beneficiaries: local chief executives and authorized approvers
OCD/NDRRMC and partner agencies receiving reports
residents, including persons with disabilities and people with limited connectivity
mechanisms: Structured fields, validation states, acknowledgement, and version history may reduce missing context and make corrections traceable.
Role-based routing and explicit human approval may shorten administrative handoffs while preserving statutory responsibility.
Provenance, immutable audit history, and portable exports may improve accountability, evidential reliability, auditability, and continuity when staff or vendors change.
Interoperable schemas and secure APIs may reduce repeated encoding, conditional on data-sharing authority and compatible government systems.
Offline capture, accessible interfaces, and manual fallback may reduce exclusion during connectivity or service failures.
prerequisites_and_possible_harms: Benefits require current official templates, trained users, reliable upstream data, maintained integrations, funded support, and government ownership of approvals and records policy.
Automation can accelerate an incorrect or unverified report; the interface must visibly distinguish draft, reported, verified, approved, superseded, and official-warning states.

Centralization can increase breach, surveillance, re-identification, and outage impact; minimization, segregation, encryption, least privilege, logging, tested recovery, and purpose-bound sharing are required.
Digital-only delivery can exclude affected communities and field staff; alternative electronic and manual channels must remain available.
Outcome claims such as faster response, fewer casualties, or improved allocation require prospective comparative evidence and cannot be inferred from feature completion or user satisfaction alone.

government_customer.creation_and_verification: Defines official forms, authorized originators, validation rules, evidentiary requirements, and who may verify field reports.
government_customer.approval_and_decisions: Retains approval of plans/reports and all statutory warnings, evacuation, calamity, funding, command, and disclosure decisions.
government_customer.custody_access_retention_disposition: Acts as controlling office/custodian; classifies access, applies approved retention schedules and legal holds, secures NAP authority where required, and authorizes transfer or disposal.
government_customer.interoperability_and_security: Authorizes recipients and purposes, approves integrations, completes required impact/risk assessments, and accepts residual operational risk.
government_customer.offboarding: Designates successor repository and confirms complete, intelligible transfer before authorizing deletion of vendor copies.

startup_provider.processing_and_support: Processes only documented instructions, implements configured workflows, trains/supports users, and does not present drafts or analytics as official decisions.
startup_provider.technical_controls: Maintains tenant isolation, least privilege, encryption, logs, versioning, backups, recovery, vulnerability management, incident notification, and availability commitments.
startup_provider.records_and_export: Preserves provenance and integrity, prevents unauthorized disposal, supplies complete portable exports, and documents transformations and migrations.
startup_provider.disclosure: Does not publish, share, or reuse government data except as authorized by the controlling agency and applicable law.
startup_provider.offboarding: Assists migration, returns data and metadata, preserves records under hold, and deletes remaining copies only after written authority and verification.

authority_and_responsibility_matrix.shared_but_not_transferred: Configuration, testing, incident exercises, schema mapping, and continuity planning may be collaborative; accountability assigned by statute to public officials and agencies is not delegated merely by procurement or software use.

lifecycle: Create/ingest with stable record ID, tenant, jurisdiction, hazard/incident ID, source agency/person/system, source URL or message identifier, received/created timestamps, and original payload.
Classify as draft, submitted, acknowledged, under verification, verified, approved, rejected, superseded, final, archived, or disposed; keep status and authority distinct from factual content.
Preserve every version and correction relationship; never overwrite the original official advisory or finalized report.
Authenticate users and approvals; retain evidence of signing/approval method, intent, time, and document version.
Apply agency/NAP-approved access and retention rules, legal holds, archival transfer, and written disposal authorization; record the actor, authority, scope, method, and result.
On offboarding, export data, attachments, schemas, audit logs, access/retention labels, and integrity evidence; obtain customer acceptance before authorized deletion.
interoperability: Use versioned, documented, non-proprietary exchange representations with stable identifiers, enumerated verification states, explicit timezone/precision, and code-list provenance.
Provide authenticated, least-privilege APIs with purpose and recipient controls, acknowledgements, idempotency keys, rate limits, error reconciliation, and complete exchange logs.
Map rather than silently normalize source terminology; retain original values and transformation rules so exported records remain explainable.
Treat DICT's government interoperability framework and customer-designated schemas as controlling when issued; do not claim national interoperability from a proprietary API alone.

risk_continuity_and_inclusion: Privacy and re-identification: minimize personal and precise location data, segregate sensitive attachments, enforce purpose-bound access, and conduct the required privacy impact assessment before production processing.
Tenant leakage: test authorization at every object and export boundary; use tenant-scoped identifiers, storage, keys where appropriate, and audit alerts for anomalous access.

Security and critical-service disruption: apply DICT/customer standards, pre-deployment and periodic security testing, prompt incident notification, offline/manual fallback, redundant backups, and restoration exercises.

Provider failure and lock-in: require escrow or documented deployment configuration where appropriate, open exports, migration assistance, defined support termination, and verified handover to the government-selected repository.

Connectivity exclusion: support low-bandwidth pages, resumable uploads, store-and-forward operation, SMS/phone/paper-assisted fallback where authorized, and reconciliation without duplicate official records.

Accessibility: conform to applicable Philippine Web Accessibility rules and test keyboard, screen-reader, contrast, error-identification, mobile, and language/reading-level needs with representative users.

Bias and false certainty: do not turn incomplete reports or analytics into automatic risk, priority, warning, or eligibility decisions; display provenance, uncertainty, missingness, and human reviewer responsibility.

Warning integrity: ingest and redistribute only authorized source messages through approved channels; preserve wording and version, identify the issuing authority, and prevent vendor branding or AI-generated text from appearing to be an official warning.
